questions.q: With the defaults $|A| = 6$ at 35° and $|B| = 5$ at 0°, what is $A \cdot B$?
questions.explain: $A \cdot B = |A|\,|B|\cos\theta = 6 \cdot 5 \cdot \cos 35° \approx 24.57$. $4.91$ is the signed shadow length $A \cdot B / |B|$, not the dot product.

questions.q: Click the **Sideways strangers** preset ($A$ at 90°, $B$ at 0°). What is the dot product?
questions.explain: $\cos 90° = 0$: the shadow of $A$ on $B$ disappears, so the dot product is 0 whatever the lengths are.

questions.q: When is the dot product of two non-zero vectors **negative**?
options: When the angle is less than 90°
When one of the vectors is longer than the other
When the angle between them is more than 90° (the shadow points against $B$)
Never — it is a length, so it is always positive
questions.explain: The sign comes from $\cos\theta$, which is negative for obtuse angles; the lengths only scale the magnitude.
